title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: second — infant elect without foresight faith; Augustine vs Pelagians
pass_a_gloss: Now as to the latter, namely the conformity of predestination among the members themselves: it is clear that many members of Christ were predestinated unto eternal life without an antecedent intuition of faith or perseverance in the same. For since persevering faith is not considered except in those who use reason and free choice, as many as dying in infancy are saved, it is necessary that they were destined to salvation without this intuition. But many die at that age, of whose salvation the Church never doubted. Many therefore both were elected and saved, in whom this foresight of faith and perseverance could have no place. By this argument drawn from elect infants Augustine everywhere shuts the mouths of the Pelagians, who established predestination to life from foresighted merits: On Predestination and Grace ch. 7; On the Gift of Perseverance ch. 8 and 12; On the Merits and Remission of Sins book 1 ch. 21; Against Two Letters of the Pelagians book 2 ch. 7.
pass_b_english: Second limb — conformity among the members: many of Christ's members were predestined to eternal life with no prior regard to faith or perseverance. Persevering faith is only considered in those who use reason and free choice; so all who die in infancy and are saved must have been destined to salvation without that regard. Many die at that age whose salvation the Church never doubted. Many, then, were both elect and saved in whom foresight of faith and perseverance could have no place. By elect infants Augustine everywhere stops the Pelagians' mouths — those who grounded predestination to life in foresighted merits (On Predestination and Grace 7; On the Gift of Perseverance 8, 12; On Merits and Remission 1.21; Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 2.7).
source_text: Jam quod ad posterius, nempe conformitatem praedestinationis inter ipsa membra: clarum est multa membra Christi in vitam aeternam fuisse praedestinata absque antecedaneo intuitu fidei aut perseverantiae in eadem. Nam cum fides perseverans non consideretur nisi in illis qui utuntur ratione et libero arbitrio, quotquot in infantia morientes salvantur, absque hujus intuitu ad salutem fuisse destinatos est necesse. At multi ea aetate moriuntur, de quorum salute Ecclesia nunquam dubitavit. Multi ergo et electi et servati fuerunt, in quibus haec praevisio fidei et perseverantiae locum habere non potuit. Hoc argumento ab infantibus electis petito Augustinus passim occludit ora Pelagianorum, qui ex praevisis meritis praedestinationem ad vitam statuerunt: De praed. et grat. cap. 7; De bono persever. cap. 8 et 12; De peccat. mer. et remiss. lib. 1. cap. 21; Contr. 2 Epist. Pelag. lib. 2. cap. 7.
